core_obligations: Observe that $(i')^*$ is defined, because $(\mathcal{O}_{X'}, s', i' : D' \to X')$ is a triple as in the definition of the Gysin homomorphism, so the statement makes sense (proof lines 5964-5966).

Set $\mathcal{L}_1 = \mathcal{O}_X$, $\mathcal{L}_2 = \mathcal{L}$ and apply the decomposition lemma to the section $s$ of $\mathcal{L}_1 \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{L}_2$, taking $D' = D_1$ (proof lines 5968-5972).

Read off the four listed properties, and their persistence under arbitrary locally finite type base change $Y \to X$, from the decomposition lemma, its formulae and the injectivity statement (proof lines 5972-5975).
proof_roadmap: Well-definedness of the deformed Gysin map (proof lines 5964-5966).
Choice of the deformation via the section decomposition (proof lines 5968-5972).
The four properties and their base change stability from the decomposition formulae and injectivity (proof lines 5972-5975).
difficulty_reason: The lemma deforms a triple to one where the divisor is the zero scheme of a single global function, with the two maps of finite type and flat of relative dimension one, injective pullback on Chow groups and the compatibility $p^*i^* = (i')^*g^*$, all of this stable under locally of finite type base change (statement lines 5939-5961). The proof is an assembly: it applies the decomposition of the section of the tensor product, takes the first component as the new divisor, and collects the four properties from that lemma, its formulae and the injectivity result. The setup of the deformation and the reading off of the listed properties are the substance, so the claim is H2.
